name: Prestige Tree Service
niche: tree service / arboriculture (removal, trimming, stump grinding, storm cleanup, cat & animal rescue)
address: 683 NW 30th St, Miami, FL 33127, United States
address_note: This is the real, current address on the business's own Google Business Profile, fetched live with Playwright (node scripts/gmaps_detail.js). It is in Miami (Allapattah/Wynwood industrial corridor), NOT Coral Gables. The task brief's working city label was 'Coral Gables, FL' with an explicit instruction to confirm the real service area from the profile; the profile itself gives Miami, FL 33127 as the address, so that is what was used for the JSON-LD, footer and map embed on the site. Copy on the site describes the service area as 'Miami, FL and Miami-Dade County' rather than naming Coral Gables specifically, since no review or source ties this business to Coral Gables.
email_search_log: No email found. Google Business Profile shows no website (website field null, 'Add website' prompt visible to owner view), so there is no domain-based email to check. No Facebook or Instagram page could be verified for this specific business via web search. Prior brand name 'Spider-Man Tree Service' (same phone number, visible on truck signage in several Google Maps photos) was also searched; no public email surfaced for that name either.
hours: Open 24 hours, every day of the week (Google Business Profile hours block, all 7 days), corroborated by truck signage reading '24 HOUR EMERGENCY SERVICE' and by review text describing a late-night cat rescue.

reviews_note: Captured live via node scripts/gmaps_reviews.js against the exact Maps place URL. Google truncates long review text with an ellipsis in this DOM view; the quotes used on the site were trimmed back to the last complete sentence before the cut (a verbatim substring of the real review, never paraphrased or completed/invented past what was captured). Anyela Gutierrez's review was NOT used on the site because it names the business's prior brand 'Spider Man Tree Service' explicitly, which would be confusing on a site branded Prestige Tree Service; it is recorded here for completeness and corroborates the rebrand.
rebrand_note: Multiple Google Maps photos of the business's own bucket truck and dump truck show the old business name 'Spider-Man Tree Service' with the SAME phone number, (786) 344-8923, as the current 'Prestige Tree Service' Google Business Profile, and two reviews refer to the owner as 'Rene'/'Renee' and to 'Spider Man Tree Service' / 'Spider-Man Tree Services' by name. This indicates the business rebranded from Spider-Man Tree Service to Prestige Tree Service while keeping the same phone number, owner and fleet. The old-brand truck photos (2 of the 9 downloaded) were excluded from the site's gallery/hero/about to avoid showing a different, superseded business name on the Prestige-branded demo.
services_evidence: Truck signage (own fleet, photographed on Google Maps) lists: Tree Trimming, Tree Removal, Stump Removal, Storm Cleanup, Garbage Removal & Recycling, Hauling Service, Excavation Service, Equipment Rentals, 24 Hour Emergency Service.

Google's own review-topic tags for this listing: 'palm tree trimming' (4 reviews), 'tree pruning' (8 reviews), 'cat rescue' (12 reviews), 'animal rescue' (7 reviews), 'warehouse roof rescue' (2 reviews), 'courteous team' (6 reviews), 'landscaping needs' (3 reviews), 'fair quote' (2), 'affordable' (3).
Full verbatim review text independently confirms tree trimming near roofs (Alan Piggot) and emergency cat/animal rescue from trees and roofs (Fefi Guzman, Jenny Lizarraga).

'new roof' (5 reviews) and 'warehouse roof rescue' (2 reviews) topic tags were NOT used as evidence of a roofing/roof-installation service on the site: no verbatim review text was captured to confirm what those tags actually refer to, so per the no-invention rule they were left out rather than guessed at.

website_check.google_business_profile: Google Maps detail view (node scripts/gmaps_detail.js, live Playwright fetch) returns website: null and shows the 'Add website' prompt in the profile's own UI text, the standard signal that the OWNER has not listed a website.
domains_tried: prestigetreeservice.com: resolves (HTTP 301) but redirects to https://www.treeandstumpservice.com.au/, an unrelated Australian company ('Prestige Tree and Stump Service', .com.au). Not this business.

prestige-tree-service.com, prestigetreeservicemiami.com, prestigetreeservicecoralgables.com: could not be reached from this sandbox (egress proxy connect_rejected on all three), treated as not confirmable rather than assumed absent; the Google profile's own missing-website signal is the primary evidence.
website_check.web_search: WebSearch for "Prestige Tree Service" Coral Gables / Miami Facebook / Instagram returned only auto-generated third-party SEO template pages (prestigetreeservice.pages.dev, .vercel.app, and dozens of similarly-templated competitor domains serving generated per-city landing pages), none of which are owned or controlled by this business; no real owned website, Facebook page or Instagram account was found.

language_signal: All captured reviews are in English; Miami English-language market business per task brief. html lang=en default, full Spanish data-es translation included per DESIGN.md bilingual rule.
photos_source: 9 photos extracted from the Google Maps listing via node scripts/gmaps_photocycle.js (Playwright photo-viewer cycling) against the exact place URL, downloaded and verified with scripts/_gmaps_photos.py (curl + PIL verify, all 9 valid, non-empty JPEGs). All 9 visually inspected one by one with the Read tool via the generated _sheet.jpg contact sheet and individually. 2 (duplicate near-identical aerial drone shots) were deduplicated to 1. 2 more (clear, legible 'Spider-Man Tree Service' truck signage, old brand name) were excluded from the build per rebrand_note above. 6 real, distinct, non-watermarked work photos were used across hero/about/gallery/avatar: aerial drone shot of a bucket truck trimming a tree between two homes; crew rigging ropes in a backyard tree; a freshly pruned set of three royal palms; a bucket truck reaching into tall royal palms over a street; a crew member grinding a stump in full safety gear; a skid steer with a grapple attachment clearing an uprooted storm-damaged tree from a street.
